global.headline: WASHINGTON REBUILDS ITS TARIFFS COUNTRY BY COUNTRY, AND NAMES FOURTEEN
summary: The US Trade Representative ruled in 14 of the 16 Section 301 investigations opened on 11 March into "structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing", proposing duties set economy by economy rather than one blanket levy. China draws the highest rate, 20 per cent, which Jamieson Greer said sits on top of the roughly 25 per cent imposed in 2018 on about two-thirds of Chinese imports. The EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland and Taiwan are held to 15 per cent, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand to 18, Vietnam to 35, India to 25 or 17 with a trade deal, and Singapore to 20, or 10 with an agreement on reciprocal trade. Mexico and Norway were investigated and spared. Some US$30 billion of Chinese goods up for cuts under the bilateral Board of Trade mechanism is exempt.

Comments close on 5 January, hearings are set for 25 January, and Greer told CNBC the duties probably will not bite for months. It rebuilds the tariffs the Supreme Court struck down on 20 February as an unlawful use of emergency powers, after which Trump fell back on Section 122's 10 per cent for 150 days. Greer said anything above 20 per cent would be read in Beijing as breaching the year-old truce, which expires on 10 January. Guo Jiakun called overcapacity "a false issue" used "as an excuse for political manipulation"; no retaliation was announced.
global.geopolitical: The instrument has changed, and with it the leverage: emergency powers set one rate for everyone and lost in court, while Section 301 attaches to every country both a rate and a lower number conditional on a deal.
global.socioeconomic: The rates tax the export model rather than particular goods, and they stack: Singapore's 20 per cent would sit above the 12.5 per cent forced-labour duty in force since 24 July. Nothing applies for two months.

global.headline: THE VICE PRESIDENT SAYS THERE WAS NO INVESTIGATION AS CONGRESS IS BRIEFED ON A SPY SERVICE
summary: JD Vance, in Dayton, Ohio, said officials had assured him Nvidia's restored chief executive was not under investigation and that "the accusations against him were based on anonymous reporting, not on actual evidence". He named Attorney General Todd Blanche among "multiple people" who gave those assurances, a day after Blanche met a question about whether Jensen Huang had been investigated with "For what?" Trump told the New York Post a pardon was "always an option, I guess, but I don't think it'll be necessary"; Vance said Huang needs none.

Officials briefing congressional staff on Tuesday said US intelligence believes Alice Huang, the Megaspeed executive, was introduced last year through a mutual friend to an officer of China's Ministry of State Security who openly deals with large companies in China, and that a man believed to be her husband was a Chinese asset in regular contact with the ministry; they cited no intelligence that she passed Nvidia material to him. Huang testifies publicly and behind closed doors next week. S&P Global placed Nvidia on CreditWatch Negative, signalling a high likelihood of downgrade, because the resignation and reinstatement "does not sufficiently answer its questions regarding board oversight of the executive code of conduct". Moody's left the Aa1 rating and stable outlook intact, saying the return cuts near-term uncertainty without resolving governance and regulatory questions.
global.geopolitical: An administration has put its own word, not a document, behind the clearance of one executive, while the intelligence given to Congress describes a contact chain into a foreign service nobody denies.
global.socioeconomic: Two agencies read the same week in opposite directions: Moody's prices the leader, S&P the board that removed and restored him in ten days. Governance, not chip demand, is now Nvidia's cost-of-capital risk.

global.headline: IRAN TURNS HORMUZ INTO A PERMISSION SYSTEM AND SAYS MINES ENFORCE IT
summary: The Revolutionary Guards' navy said two oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire early on Wednesday east of the strait after taking what it called an unauthorised route; some Iranian accounts say three vessels, including an LNG carrier. No ship was named, no flag state or crew casualties given, and none of it independently confirmed — the Joint Maritime Information Centre has called comparable claims unconfirmed and the US military has disputed earlier mine reports. Iran's army said it had upgraded surveillance and warned that ships crossing without coordinating with Iranian forces were running greater risks; Tehran Times reported two American drones shot down over the waterway.

Tehran now ties reopening to the lifting of the US naval blockade of Iranian ports, on top of its seven earlier conditions, and the army chief's order to close the strait "further day by day" until Washington meets them stands. Trump says the next decision on fresh strikes can wait until after the new year while a deal remains reachable, and that no talks are under way; Iran's foreign ministry agrees. Qatar is pressing Washington to revive them.
global.geopolitical: Requiring ships to coordinate passage converts a blockade into an administrative claim over an international strait: a sovereignty assertion, not a siege. Mines make it self-enforcing and deniable at once.
global.socioeconomic: Unattributed mines are harder to price than missiles — no aggressor to exclude, no confirmed incident to rate. Owners must choose between a permission regime that legitimises Tehran's claim and cover against a hazard nobody confirms.

global.headline: ISRAEL'S COURT TELLS THE PROSECUTION ITS BRIBERY CASE WILL NOT STAND
summary: Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara, summoned to a hearing she rarely attends, that conviction in Case 4000 was unlikely and the case should be dropped: "There is serious doubt as to whether the evidentiary foundation supports this allegation." They cited shifts in the account of the key witness Shlomo Filber and a timeline that did not hold; of Case 2000 they had "serious doubts as to whether the conduct described in the indictment actually constitutes a criminal offence"; in Case 1000, the cigars and champagne, they urged a negotiated end. None of it is a ruling. Case 4000 alleged regulatory favours to Shaul Elovitch's Bezeq for favourable coverage on Walla!, put at more than 1 billion shekels (about S$384 million) by CNN and about 1.8 billion by Reuters.

Baharav-Miara said she would review every recommendation and that only "a verdict or an appropriate plea agreement" can end the matter. Netanyahu, at the Knesset, called it vindication after "10 years of terrible suffering", said "this trial needs to end immediately" and repeated his offer of a unity government; Israel Katz said a trial "tainted from the outset" should close. He was indicted in January 2020 and began testifying in December 2024. Gadi Eisenkot, who holds the mandate, has set 6 December as his deadline to form a government, and Avigdor Liberman said he is on track.
global.geopolitical: The case was the fixed point of Israeli politics: every coalition since 2020 was assembled around a defendant. Remove the bribery count and the reason rivals would not sit with him goes too.
global.socioeconomic: Nothing was decided, and that is the cost. A court that doubts the indictment in public but issues no judgment leaves the attorney general choosing between a verdict years away and a deal resembling surrender.

global.headline: AMERICA GREW AT 4.3 PER CENT AND ITS INFLATION WENT UP WITH IT
summary: The Commerce Department revised third-quarter growth to an annualised 4.3 per cent from the 3.4 first reported, the best quarter in three years, with business investment — software above all, the signature of AI building — the largest driver, and consumer spending central too. The Federal Reserve's preferred gauge moved the other way: personal consumption expenditures prices accelerated to 3.8 per cent annualised in October from 3.7, nearly double the 2 per cent target, though the monthly pace eased to 0.3 from September's 0.5. Strip that out and real spending was flat for the month. The savings rate rose half a point to 4.1 per cent, against 4.9 a year earlier, and much of October's income gain came from Medicare rebates. "The cautious consumer is back," wrote Heather Long of Navy Federal.

Markets took it badly, then recovered most of it. Shares opened sharply lower on AI selling, the Nasdaq Composite down close to 4 per cent and the Dow off more than 1,100 points, before paring back: the Dow closed up 0.33 per cent at 50,182.95, the S&P 500 down about 0.25 per cent near 7,182.78, the Nasdaq down 0.62 per cent at 23,585.80. Nvidia fell 3.91 per cent to US$149.30, a second straight decline.
global.geopolitical: A central bank pushed towards raising rates while most peers cut pulls capital to the dollar and tightens conditions for every borrower priced off it. The economies just handed tariff rates meet both at once.
global.socioeconomic: Growth is coming from firms buying software, not households being better off: real spending flat, savings thinner than a year ago. A December rate rise would add mortgage and card costs on top of 3.8 per cent inflation.

singapore.headline: CIVIL SERVANTS GET TWO MONTHS AS THE OFFICIAL GROWTH FORECAST GOES TO SIX PER CENT
summary: The Public Service Division announced a 1.55-month year-end bonus for all civil servants, up from 1.3 months in 2025, taking the annual variable component to two months for 2026 with June's 0.45-month mid-year payment. Grades equivalent to MX13(I) and MX14 receive a one-off S$300, and MX15, MX16 and the Operations Support Scheme S$600, in line with National Wages Council recommendations to lift lower-wage pay; the one-month non-pensionable annual allowance continues.

The payment rests on a growth forecast now put at around 6 per cent for 2026, against the 4.5 to 5.5 per cent range given in August. The division cited better-than-expected performance over the first three quarters and an expectation that the global boom in AI-related investment runs to the end of the year, benefiting manufacturing and wholesale trade, alongside the Manpower Ministry's third-quarter advance release showing stronger employment growth with unemployment and retrenchments edging up slightly. NTUC's Cham Hui Fong called the support "progressive and targeted" while warning of structural shifts from AI and digitalisation.
singapore.geopolitical: The forecast that sets the state's own wage bill now turns on AI capital spending abroad, in the same chip trade as the American enforcement actions naming Singapore-registered firms.
singapore.socioeconomic: Two months is the clearest signal that the government expects the upswing to hold into 2027, while the flat payments to junior grades concede the aggregate number is not reaching the bottom of the scale.

singapore.headline: THE CHIEF JUSTICE MARKS OUT WHERE A COURT STOPS AND PARLIAMENT BEGINS
summary: Sundaresh Menon, who retires in February 2027, used his keynote at the Global Rule of Law Conference to argue that a judgment prompting a Cabinet review, a consultation or a new statute does not mean the judiciary has taken on a political function. His example was the Sentencing (Scams) Bill, introduced on 3 November after the High Court in September allowed the appeals of four scam offenders who offended under 21, replacing reformative training with probation of a year to 18 months; the Bill would make jail or reformative training the default for young scam mules.

He also cited Tan Seet Eng, detained without trial in 2013 under the Criminal Law (Temporary Provisions) Act, whose order the Court of Appeal set aside for failing to establish harm in Singapore: the Home Affairs Ministry then reviewed other detentions and released three detainees no court had ordered freed. "Neither institution assumed the function of the other, but each responded within its proper constitutional lane," Menon said of that sequence, adding that "authoritative judicial determinations must be respected by those branches". Section 377A went the same way: challenges dismissed on procedural grounds but with a note that equality jurisprudence could affect a future case, after which the Attorney-General advised the provision was at significant risk and repeal followed consultations.
singapore.geopolitical: Singapore is making a claim about method rather than values: a court enforcing statutory limits and a legislature rewriting the statute afterwards is dialogue, not conflict — a communitarian model argued before an international audience.
singapore.socioeconomic: For anyone litigating against the state here, a win can be answered by legislation within two months, as the scam-mule appeals were, but it can also free people no court was asked about.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE'S MARINE LAB BECOMES A REGIONAL INSTRUMENT BEFORE THE NEXT BLEACHING
summary: St John's Island National Marine Laboratory was renamed the National Marine Research Station and given the lead of a new South-east Asia Marine Research Stations Network, launched by President Tharman Shanmugaratnam at the start of Marine Science Week on its tenth anniversary. More than 10 stations from Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines have joined, and the NUS-hosted station will open its facilities, data and expertise to the region, beginning with shared sea temperatures.

Director Jani Tanzil said sea warming is the region's biggest challenge and the network could detect early signs of the fifth global coral bleaching event, forecast for April to July 2027 after one of the strongest El Niño events; the previous four were in 1998, 2010, 2016 and 2024, the last the most intense on record, reaching reefs in more than 80 countries and territories. Singapore's three research buoys already report in near real time through the Marine Environment Sensing Network. Within five years it will add imaging instruments to identify plankton, the first organisms to react to environmental shifts and the precursor of harmful algal blooms, and a vessel to replace an 18-year-old boat, under the S$37 billion Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2030 plan.
singapore.geopolitical: Scientific infrastructure is the cheapest form of regional convening, and Singapore has taken the chair of it a year before the ASEAN chair. A shared temperature series is also a shared evidentiary record.
singapore.socioeconomic: A bleaching event with a forecast window is a planning problem, not a disaster: reefs are nurseries for fished stocks and coastal barriers, so monitoring changes what fisheries and coastal works can prepare for.

word.definition: A remark a judge makes in passing which forms no part of the binding decision, and so carries persuasive weight without legal force.
word.etymology: Latin, "a thing said by the way", from obiter, in passing, and dictum, something said; used in English law since the eighteenth century in contrast to the ratio decidendi, the reasoning that actually binds.
word.example: The Jerusalem court was explicit that its advice to drop the bribery case was obiter dictum and no judgment at all, which did not stop Netanyahu from treating it as vindication and demanding the trial end immediately.
